They contribute to a definition; they are not definitional. The minimum data set itself (Table 3, the data-element sheets, Tables 6-7) is deliberately NOT extracted, modelled or made computable, per the owner. Governance, financing, staffing and data-submission duties (steps a, c, d, f, g, h, l; Annex B clauses 1-11 and 14) are organisational, not system requirements, and are left out. The system type each requirement belongs to is recorded in glossary/hrhis-registry-2015.glossary.json. Nothing here is folio content until an L2 folio cites it.

candidates.statement: In a national context an electronic health workforce registry can be considered the single authoritative source of health workforce information that can provide an accurate count of all health care personnel that either have worked or are currently working at national or sub-national levels, including in the private sector.
candidates.section_title: Health workforce registry – concept and function

candidates.statement: An electronic health workforce registry can be designed to authenticate and validate the existence of a health worker and provide essential details about that person.
candidates.section_title: Health workforce registry – concept and function

candidates.statement: In addition, a health workforce registry can ensure quality control, provide easy access to information on production, distribution and utilization of health personnel, and assist in budgeting, research development and advocacy.
candidates.section_title: Health workforce registry – concept and function

candidates.statement: A health workforce registry allows aggregation of health workforce data in several combinations and assists both national and sub-national ministries of health in producing essential indicator-based reports, as needed.
candidates.section_title: Health workforce registry – concept and function

candidates.statement: The health workforce registry is a central and essential component of a functional HRIS, as it contains important health worker attributes that can subsequently be linked to other relevant HRIS components.
candidates.section_title: Health workforce registry – concept and function

candidates.name: Address policy and governance mechanism
candidates.statement: In addition, a clear policy articulating rules-based algorithms for data validation and de-duplication must be in place. Necessary and sufficient data access controls must be instituted based on an agreed policy to address data privacy, security, confidentiality and meaningful use.
candidates.section_title: Telephone number

candidates.name: Agree on a location to operate the registry
candidates.statement: For general management of health workforce data, it is recommended that the health workforce registry be placed at national level with adequate access at sub-national levels for both authorized data access and data submission.
candidates.section_title: Telephone number

candidates.name: Assure privacy, security and confidentiality of health workforce data
candidates.statement: It is essential that adequate privacy, security and confidentiality of health workforce data be enforced at all levels of data transaction. Modern electronic health workforce registry design must assure sufficient data protection without preventing data use. In addition, sufficient security of both electronic data and related physical assets must be ensured to guard from theft and misuse.

candidates.statement: Based on stakeholder input, a standardized list of reports must be programmed as part of the software design to generate accurate and timely reports.

candidates.name: Develop, test, and deploy a functional electronic health workforce registry
candidates.statement: While designing the electronic health workforce registry, adhere to best practices in information systems design to assure accuracy, timeliness, completeness, reliability, privacy, security, and confidentiality of the data and information systems and assets. Test and validate all data within the registry before it becomes fully operational. Full consideration must be given to all interoperability issues, in order to ensure that data from the registry can easily be transported to existing health workforce information systems or larger health information systems.

candidates.statement: The registry shall conform to best practices in information systems design in order to assure quality, accuracy, timeliness, completeness, reliability, privacy, security, and confidentiality of the data and information systems and assets.
candidates.section_title: Sample components of the registry operational framework

candidates.statement: Legally authorized users of the registry shall be required to have unique user names and passwords that will be provided by the national Steering Committee, on the approval of the highest health authority at national and sub-national levels. Level of access to the registry shall be determined by the national Steering Committee or its authorized agent.
candidates.section_title: Sample components of the registry operational framework

candidates.statement: The registry must be in compliance with all applicable national and sub-national laws related to privacy, security, and confidentiality of data.
candidates.section_title: Sample components of the registry operational framework

candidates.statement: The registry and its related physical assets shall be secured in accordance with applicable national and sub-national laws.
